DM: So okay, so, I mean, you're having to tack across the wind. But Wellby is a good— good sailor, good enough sailor. You managed to make, you know, by—by noon, another, like, 4 h, you manage to make another, like, 28 miles of progress, like out now in the middle of the ocean.
DM: And so by the time the sun is set, you've traveled another probably almost 50 miles, so a total of a total of something like 80-ish miles. And you.
DM: So that's 1, 2— and have, based on Wellby’s dead reckoning, find yourself as the sun is setting— of a—this view is not of sunset, but seeing in the distance a rocky coast.
DM: So you settle into a small cove for the evening.
DM: Okay, so, as you make dinner and settle in, presumably on the shore. There’s not really a lot of—there’s not really enough space for you to sleep on the boat. That's too small.

markers.reading: Fly up to a hill lookout, scout the coast and town, then return down to the companions at the cove.

Presumably I can get relatively high, like towards the tops of one of these hills, and then just look around. Is there any towns? Any signs of—?
DM: So there is—there is a small city, town-ish, something like that, that’s actually back a little ways along the coast that you sailed past, maybe 50 miles or so. Didn’t—

route.reading: Scout from higher ground near the cove; return down after the observations.

markers.reading: From the hill, see a smaller fishing town back along the coast; the estimate is corrected to about fifteen miles east.

evidence.quote: DM: So there is—there is a small city, town-ish, something like that, that’s actually back a little ways along the coast that you sailed past, maybe 50 miles or so. Didn’t—

markers.reading: Scry the fishing town’s docks, hearing ordinary trade and unease about war and seeing a Legion patrol.

evidence.quote: Delwath: Scrying on the docks now that I can see it, which is the next thing I'm gonna do.

DM: Okay, so you see the docks. You know, most of it is just kind of the normal bustle. There’s—there’s people hauling fish, you know a little bit of chatter back and forth, people talking Chardonian. And do you speak Chardonian?

DM: There’s definitely a lot of chatter about Chardon, like not in any clear way, right? You don’t hear your names mentioned. You don’t hear, you know, “So Kenzo and Delwath escaped from their execution and are the most wanted.” But there’s a lot of chatter about, like, “What happens? Like, is there gonna be war? Who did this?” Like, you know, things are bad. “Is—you know, are they gonna—is there gonna be a tax? Is there gonna be a levy? Are we gonna get drafted into the navy?”
DM: But there is a guard. I mean, there is a guard here. You do, like— you do see in the 10 min the Chardonian Legion patrolling the dock.

markers.reading: The next morning, sail about eight miles east and stop in a second cove short of Artevus.

evidence.quote: DM: You're currently sailing the big boat into town, which is about 10 miles back east. Okay. So, correct.
Delwath: Morning we embiggened the boat, and we sailed 8 miles or so back along the coast. That’s probably, what, an hour and a half or something. Yeah, so—
DM: Something like that.

Delwath: And when we got sort of not quite, like, obviously within sight of town, right? We’re hugging the coast when we’re close to town, but not, like, “Hey, the town can see the boat” close. We find a little cove with a not-sheer cliff, and Delwath and Kenzo, I guess, scramble up to the— how are you not going to get recognized, Kenzo? Do you have a disguise ability?

distance.basis: Accepted retrospective account of the completed morning leg.

duration.basis: Accepted retrospective duration, approximately an hour and a half.

markers.reading: Go alone from the near-town cove, down the rocks through Artevus’s main square, and into the inn.

evidence.quote: Kenzo: And maybe not me.
Kenzo: Oh, yeah, that's right. We are the 2 terrorists. Fine.
Delwath: I can go by myself. It’s fine. Does our telepathy last that range?
DM: So you, as you approach from the cliff side, you can see basically what you saw before. The town's like fairly quiet in the morning.

DM: So you kind of make your way—pick your way down the rocks into the sort of main square, definitely getting some looks. It's small enough that everybody kinda knows everybody in town. So you know, them— rumor, or the sort of chatter starts going around like, “Oh, there’s a stranger in town.” It's big enough that you're not immediately questioned, but small enough that it's obvious you're not like from here.
Delwath: So I'll go to the inn. I mean the—

Delwath: I'll start at the inn. I mean, I I don't need to like play out every moment in detail, but the basic idea is to kind of spend money right? I brought a bunch of gold. I don't know. We have tons of gold, right? Lots of mixed coins, right? So I can—I mean, pay out silver, not just gold.
DM: So you spend a little—a little—wait, a little while, maybe an hour or so, just kind of sitting in the inn.

route.reading: Enter the town through the rocks and main square.

markers.reading: Approach Summer’s Breeze with the companions’ boat, tie alongside, and climb aboard to meet the captain.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, so you're heading up to Martino. The rest of you are sailing. So when you get close, you can see the ship. It’s a— it’s a reasonably—
Wellby: I’ll sort of, like, hail the captain or mate or whoever I can see on deck telepathically, and come out and give him a wave and ask, “Come aboard?”

DM: She is a sort of stout halfling, wearing a wide-brimmed hat, green—green cloak, like, nice boots, curly brownish hair underneath the hat, smile on her face. Just kind of looking out over the rail, and when she realized you’re a halfling she, like, gives you a big wave, and you can see the ships called the Summer’s Breeze. It seems—the ship seems pretty quiet, actually. Not—
Wellby: I’ll climb aboard, and, like, we’ll tie a little ship against theirs and—
DM: Yeah, yeah.

markers.note: Only Wellby’s boarding is explicit here; the others’ completed boarding is confirmed at l14.

markers.reading: Visit Martino at his house in the hills while the others approach the halflings.

evidence.quote: Delwath: I—while they’re sailing out, while they’re doing this, I will hike up and talk to Martino.
DM: Meanwhile, Delwath, unaware of you hiring the— yourself out as crew for the halflings, approaches the house of Martino.

DM: An old sailor, tanned skin, he’s sitting—he’s sitting on his do, basically looking out, like, Bab— whittling something. And you can see that his left hand is sort of like badly injured, like he’s got a scar down the middle, and it doesn’t really move. Right hand seems fine. I mean, he’s whittling with his right hand, tangled gray beard, and looks up as—as Delwath approaches.

markers.reading: Descend to town and swim underwater to the companions’ boat tied beside Summer’s Breeze, climbing aboard with gills and fins.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay. So you head down. You see the ship in—you see your ship dock next to the halfling ship in the harbor.
DM: It's like lunchtime at this point.
Delwath: So, so I’ll—when I— when there’s nobody looking, right, I’ll just, like, slip into the water. And then once I’m 3 quarter, you know, once I’m in the water, I’ll turn aquatic, right?

Delwath: But that—Delwath swims underwater. You’ve not seen them do this before, deep underwater at the bottom of the water, and come up by the boat right, and climb up into the boat, like, not visible from town, but with, like, gills and fins.
DM: Pippa looks at you a bit strangely. “That’s one of yours?”
Wellby: Delwath, Pippa. Pippa, Delwath. Delwath, real brief, We're gonna sail. They're gonna take us. They're gonna take us. Yeah. I—

Quiet, as you—as you come, and there’s a—a—a younger man who sort of bows and backs out as—as you approach.

DM: She looks up at me, she says, “Welcome!” And you could see, like, scattered around this study there’s, like, probably a hundred different little trinkets of various kinds, like some made of coral, some made of shell, all something, like, ocean-related.

I mean, obviously there’s, like, a handful of—I mean, there’s some blacksmith. There’s—there’s barrelwrights and things, but it’s not the sort of place that has a huge— I'll be—
DM: You know, crafting district or something like that. Like,

DM: You know, there’s the—the sort of heart of the city has, like—trade seems to be its main wealth, right? Like, there’s merchant houses, there’s— I mean, you see, like big barrels of olive oil being rolled into warehouses, and me— you know, wine and and cheese and salted fish, lots of salted fish.
DM: Yeah, Riswynn is mostly just sightseeing. I mean, you don't hear much. You don't like pick up a lot of obvious news. Kenzo and Riswynn are kind of chilling.

Seeker: And sure, you know it's the cafe.
Kenzo: Yeah.

DM: So I mean, the way—just, like, the vibe of the city, right, is like there’s, you know, cafes and inns and things and taverns along the docks. You know, there’s the rich people houses. There’s the market, like, it’s mid-afternoon at this point, so, you know, the people are starting to file into the taverns. Like, you guys are only— spend—you can certainly, like, poke around a little bit, spend a little time, like, seeing if you can—
DM: Okay, well, I mean, you do—you do pick up a bunch of rumors as you sort of wander the the the docks, mostly.

markers.reading: Spend the evening among the dockside taverns listening to merfolk songs.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, well, I mean, you do—you do pick up a bunch of rumors as you sort of wander the the the docks, mostly.
DM: If you walk around town asking about merfolk, everybody’s like, “Oh yeah, you should go listen to the ballads in the taverns.”
DM: You spend the evening.
DM: And as you wander, you hear the—
DM: Keep wandering around a little bit, poking in some other taverns.

markers.reading: Hear the popular woman’s pan-pipe ballad from a crowded tavern; the source does not settle whether the listeners enter.

evidence.quote: DM: You hear one more song: a woman who seems to have drawn quite a crowd, who’s, like, playing on—on pan pipes and—and singing a ballad echoing from from a tavern that’s, like, people are spilling out. Like, she seems to be very popular.

Recorded song: In the depths, beneath storm and ocean’s, a garden lush, when merfolk’s secrets do abide. Oh, sing of the kelp so green, rich jade lies deep and still unseen. 100 leagues, secret sleep ’neath waves of gray. A.

Recorded song: The merfolk dance with silken fins among the kelp. They tend the jade with gentle care, each name a whisper soft as air. Oh, sing of the kelp so green, rich jade lies deep and still unseen, a hundred— west o’ Tamaro Bay, where secret sleep ’neath waves of gray. A. A. A.

Recorded song: From the deep the jade does grow, glowing faint with mystic show. Names of old, names and new sprout in gardens deep and blue. Oh, sing of the kelp so green, rich jade lies deep and still unseen, a 100— sleep ’neath waves of grey. Tales are told of those who find the garden left behind. Merfolk’s whispers call, in the jade, names of all.

markers.reading: Return to Summer’s Breeze at its Castrella anchorage for the halflings’ late dinner.

evidence.quote: DM: So the night ends with you back with some more information. And now left trying to decide how you're going to convince the halflings who are now seem to be at, like, 9 pm about halfway through quite elaborate dinner.
DM: Pippa looks up and waves you over and is like, “You still hungry? We’ve got salt cod pie, we’ve got— oh, you’ve got to try this— cinnamon cakes! You ever had cinnamon?”
DM: “Comes from down south, down south of Illoria. I might even have some dried fruit from the last time that Milo came up, this fruit leather that’s sweet and tangy is amazing. Come, eat.”

markers.reading: Plan to leave Castrella around four or early dawn and sail northwest, looking for Milo and caves where the stoneborn hermit may live.

evidence.quote: DM: So I think we can end there. So as you go to bed for the night, the halflings are preparing. They need to take on—I mean, they need to restock a little bit. They need to finish their dinner and take on water and stuff. And—and so it’s gonna be first—it’s gonna be pre-dawn that they leave.

DM: But they’ve made plans to—Pippa apparently stays up all night fairly frequently, and is going to wake the—wake Wellby and the crew at 4, and get the boat underway early dawn, heading fast as can be northwest up the coast, Looking for Milo, worried that he’s lost somewhere, and keeping an eye out on the side for caves where a stoneborn hermit might live.

route.reading: Head northwest along the coast, watching for the hermit’s cave; no reached destination is established.
